title: Late-shift kernel grok and triage
content:
Quick notes while I’m grokking the kernel behavior that spiked p99 on late bursts (night reg).

Context:
- Nightly customer traffic pattern: small bursts (<=8 tokens, many short requests) from hosted-api region-us-west.
- p99 climbed ~300ms overnight on gpu-pool-a (A100s) for a subset of routes.
- Autoscaler didn't escalate because average utilization stayed under threshold.

What I observed (raw):
- p50 stable, p95 slightly up, p99 increases in sharp spikes every ~90s.
- Traces show single inference RPC waiting in the runtime process for ~200–350ms before scheduling to CUDA.
- KV cache hits seem normal for these requests; misses correlate with longer wait.
- Kernel/trace snippet: host-worker-17 local queue depth 6 -> worker stalls for 220ms with blocked syscall: epoll_wait.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Ephemeral NVLink congestion causing occasional scheduling stalls on the device queue (rare but high-latency).
2) Host-side batching scheduler emits a batch but a cgroup or CPU steal delays the dispatch thread, so CUDA enqueue is delayed.
3) A lock contention in the KV cache eviction path under small request fanout (eviction triggered by slightly higher memory pressure).
4) Network variance between control plane and worker (less likely; traces show host-local blocking).

Quick reproducer attempts I ran (commands and results):
- Reproducer script: run 200x short requests (2–8 tokens) with 0.01s inter-arrival across 8 parallel clients against dev pool.
  - Observed p99 ~ 180ms baseline; occasional 330ms spike when running on node set (gpu-pool-a subset).
- strace on runtime process around a spike: repeated epoll_wait(....) returns after ~220ms. Stack top shows scheduler thread in poll.
- perf top during spike: top symbols are epoll_wait, pthread_cond_wait, some block in runtime batcher.

Quick debug notes (things to try next):
- Add micro-instrumentation: log time between batch ready and CUDA enqueue (nanosecond resolution) for 12 hours on a canary node.
- Temporarily increase batcher priority (sched_fifo, 4) for the dispatch thread on canary to see if p99 removes the 200ms component.
- Run with CPU isolation cpuset (pin dispatch thread + python worker to dedicated cores) to rule-out CPU steal.
- Check cgroup memory swap events (oom_kill? though not killed) and kernel dmesg for 'block' messages.
- Force KV cache off for a small fraction of requests to see if spikes correlate with eviction.

Immediate actions I did (timestamped):
- 23:05 – kicked a canary with micro-instrumentation flag. Output goes to /var/log/redwood/micro-instr/late-shift-20260312.log
- 23:18 – raised thread sched priority on canary process pid 23412 (experiment) -> initial 1h run shows p99 drop by ~60ms but not eliminated.
- 23:44 – disabled KV eviction sampling on canary (quick config patch) -> no obvious change in spike frequency in first 20m.

Empirical numbers (from quick runs):
- baseline p99 (no change): 320–360ms during spike windows
- after sched priority bump: p99 spikes to 260–300ms (improvement ~60ms)
- KV eviction toggle: no measurable delta in 20m window

Notes-to-self / open questions to ping SRE / infra: 
- Does node-level kernel scheduling show any 'softirqs' backlog during spikes? Ask SRE to check /proc/softirqs and irqstat around 90s cadence.
- Are there any nightly cron jobs running on gpu-pool-a nodes? (patches, backups, monitoring gatherers) — check with infra.
- Verify NVSwitch stats (nvlink error counters) historically for the node slice.

TODO (actionable checklist):
- [ ] Deploy micro-instrumentation cluster-wide on a 5% sample (config: runtime.flag.batch_enq_timing=true, sample_rate=0.05)
- [ ] Add diagnostic metric: "dispatch_to_cuda_ms" to Datadog with p50/p95/p99
- [ ] Experiment: cpuset isolate dispatch thread + python worker on one canary node
- [ ] Run kernel 5.15->5.19 test on staging variant (if reproducer persists) to rule out scheduler differences
- [ ] Follow up with SRE about nightly tasks and possible cron collisions
- [ ] If above doesn't isolate, capture perf + ftrace for full 1m around spike and upload to GH gist

Morning handoff summary (to drop into standup):
- I'm running a canary with dispatch-thread high priority; immediate reduction in p99 amplitude but not fully resolved. Key suspects: host scheduling delays and rare device-queue stalls. Need SRE to check kernel-level interrupts and infra nightly jobs. Will expand instrumentation and add a metric to Datadog.

Other random findings / brain dump:
- If this is host scheduling, moving dispatch off the general worker pool (dedicated tiny process pinned to two cores) might fix without kernel patching. Could be a low-effort mitigation.
- If spikes coincide with NVSwitch congestion, mitigation might be to spread short-request traffic across different racks. Smart routing could be short-term fix.

End notes:
- Save log excerpt from /var/log/redwood/micro-instr/late-shift-20260312.log lines with epoll durations >150ms -> gist id TODO
- Follow up with Ishaan on kernel perf script improvements (he has perf+ftrace wrapper)

Random TODO for myself: get coffee and write up short PR with the micro-instr flag and a small Datadog metric (one-liner in runtime).

-- Mila
